dedication-f1.text: HONORATISSI- MO DOMINO NON MINUS VIRTUTE SUA, QUAM GENERIS SPLENDORE, ILLUSTRISSIMO, GEORGIO BERKLEIO, MILITI DE BALNEO, BARONI DE BERKLEY MOUBREY, SEGRAVE, D. DE BRUSE, DOMINO SUO Multis Nominibus Observando, HANC SUAM MELANCHOLIAE ANATOMEN, JAM SEXTO REVISAM, D. D. DEMOCRITUS Junior.

translations.literal: To the most honoured lord, no less by his own virtue than by the splendour of his race most illustrious, George Berkeley, knight of the Bath, baron of Berkeley, Mowbray, Segrave, lord of Bruse, his lord on many names to be respected, this his of-melancholy anatomy, now for the sixth time revised, D. D. Democritus Junior.
translations.note: A dedication in the style of an inscription. "D. D." is the usual dedicatory abbreviation for dat dedicat ("gives and dedicates"), also read as dono dedit ("has given as a gift"). "D. de Bruse" stands for Dominus de Bruse, "Lord of Bruse". "Multis nominibus" usually means "on many accounts", but after the list of titles it can also mean "under many names", which may be a light pun. Burton prints "Moubrey" for Mowbray.
translations.text: To the most honourable lord, no less illustrious for his own virtue than for the splendour of his lineage, George Berkeley, Knight of the Bath, Baron of Berkeley, Mowbray, Segrave, Lord of Bruse, his lord to be honoured on many accounts, Democritus Junior gives and dedicates this his Anatomy of Melancholy, now revised for the sixth time.
